analysis.investment_thesis: A tiny (~INR 99 Cr revenue) recently-listed capital-goods microcap riding India's infra capex cycle, with leverage of 1.16x D/E and a single blow-out FY25 (PAT 3→14 Cr) that's likely the peak being sold into IPO enthusiasm. At 11x EV/EBITDA on cyclical peak margins with no margin of safety and an untested business through a downturn, the price-to-value relationship is unfavorable.
key_strengths: FY25 inflection: EBITDA 8→18 Cr, OCF 14→15 Cr, borrowings trimmed 43→33 Cr
Exposure to durable India infra theme (metro, HDD, foundation rigs)
High promoter skin in the game at 73.05%
key_risks: FY25 looks like a cyclical peak — margins jumped from 4-5% to 18% in one year
D/E 1.16x with negligible cash; finance cost 3 Cr eats ~17% of EBITDA if cycle turns
Microcap capital-goods, founded 2016, never tested through an infra slowdown
red_flags: ROE 73.8% is optically inflated by a tiny equity base (29 Cr) — not sustainable
Net profit leapt 3→14 Cr in one year; earnings quality unproven
Recently listed in a hot SME/microcap IPO cycle — classic late-cycle tell
Zero FII participation, thin institutional validation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level thinking: the market is extrapolating FY25's sudden margin expansion (operating margin 7.4% on revenue, but EBITDA vaulted from 8 to 18 Cr) as the new normal. In reality, Indian infra-equipment makers are deeply cyclical, and a 4-year revenue CAGR of 20% masks the fact that 2024 was actually down y/y before the FY25 spike. Pay 11x EV/EBITDA on what is likely peak-of-cycle EBITDA and you are underwriting zero mean reversion — there is no margin of safety here. The balance sheet is also thinner than headline ROE suggests: 33 Cr of debt on 29 Cr equity, essentially zero cash, and FY22 OCF of -5 Cr reminds us what a working-capital squeeze looks like for this business.

Where are we in the cycle? India infra capex is at a multi-year high, SME/microcap IPO euphoria is pronounced, and this name fits the pattern of cycle-peak listings priced for perfection. The downside scenario — orders slow, margins revert to a 5-6% historical average, EBITDA halves to ~9 Cr — leaves the stock looking like 20x+ on normalized earnings with leverage. I don't see the asymmetric payoff; I see optimism already in the price with a long tail of things that can go wrong. Pass, and revisit only if the cycle cracks and price falls 40-50%.
